newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Australia Yield Spreads-Breaks 100 bp to U.S..
newsitem.headline: Australia Yield Spreads-Breaks 100 bp to U.S..

text.p: Australian bond yield spreads narrowed sharply against the dollar bloc as a firm U.S. Treasury market in Tokyo triggered off local short covering, taking yields to their lowest level since late February.
It also took the 10-year bond yield spread to the U.S. to its lowest level in over two weeks and through the psychological 100 basis point level.
Analysts were slightly bemused by the reaction to Greenspan's comments which, as usual, didn't really give a really strong clue on policy in the short-term.
He said that growth and inflation would slow in late 1997 going into 1998, but would act if this does not prove the case.
The market made a strong outperformance against Canadian debt, which while firmer with the U.S. market on Thursday, was held back by a weaker Canadian dollar.
However, the yield curve flattened once again as hopes of a further policy easing continued to be unwound following Thursday's comments by Reserve Bank governor Ian Macfarlane ruling out such a move.
